blocks.text: In biomedical science, polymers are very important for making artificial organs: man-made devices that replace or support the function of damaged or diseased parts of the body. Polymers used in the body must be biocompatible, mechanically suitable, sterilisable, durable and tunable. They must not harm the body, cause allergies or be rejected by the immune system, and their strength, flexibility or elasticity can be adjusted to match the body part they replace (flexible for blood vessels, strong for bones).

blocks.caption: Polymers in artificial organs (book's Table 26.2)
rows: smooth surfaces prevent blood clots; replace or bypass blocked vessels
highly flexible and durable; must resist clotting
a scaffold for new skin growth; some dissolve as the wound heals

blocks.prompt: Why is PTFE suitable for artificial blood vessels?
blocks.explanation: It is biocompatible and has a very smooth surface that helps prevent blood clots.

items: Medical polymers: biocompatible, suitable strength, sterilisable, durable.
PTFE/PET vessels, polyurethane/silicone valves, PLA skin, UHMWPE joints, PMMA cornea.
